Quantification of pain is one of the most important issues 
in modern anesthesia and pain medicine. Moreover, assessing 
and managing of pain could improve the quality of care 
throughout the whole treatment . In this research, we 
conducted a clinical experiment including nociceptive pain 
stimuli and evaluated heart rate variability (HRV)[1] as one of 
the possible candidates for pain quantification.

a result, significant differences (p<0.0017) were not found in

nociceptive pain stimuli. 
I. INTRODUCTION 
Quantification of pain is one of the most important issues 
in modern anesthesia and pain medicine. Moreover, assessing 
and managing of pain could improve the quality of care 
throughout the whole treatment . In this research, we 
conducted a clinical experiment including nociceptive pain 
stimuli and evaluated heart rate variability (HRV)[1] as one of 
the possible candidates for pain quantification. 
II. EXPERIMENTAL METHODS 
 This study was approved by the Asan Medical Center 
Institutional Rev iew Board (approval number: 2014 –0309) 
and register ed on an international clinical trials registry 
platform (h ttp://cris.nih.go.kr, KCT0001808 ). Ten healthy 
volunteers (7 males and 3 females, 22.8±1.5 years old) were 
participated to this research. According to the protocol , we 
applied force to the tibia , 15 cm below from the patella, to 
induce nociceptive pain. Pain stimuli were increased in 
stepwise until NRS (Numerical Rating Scale) reaches a 5 (5 
NRS). Fig. 1 shows the research protocol. Each phase of 
experimental protocol could be described as BL, baseline of a 
session (3 minute ); Sn, n-th p ain stimuli until 5 NRS 
(increment: 25N/10s); Pn, 1-minute maintenance period of 5 
NRS of n-th pain stimuli; PSIn, post-stimuli interval after Pn (≥ 
5 minute). 
Pain s timuli were repeated twice in a session with time 
interval. Randomly selected drug -remifentanil (RF) or normal 
saline (NS) - was injected by target controlled infusion (3 
ng/ml) at second phase after PSI1. The second s ession was 
conducted with the other drug after at least 2 hours break. 
Typical time domain variables , AVNN, SDNN, SDSD, 
RMSSD and pNN50 , were used for HRV analysis with 
1-minute length ECG in BL, 5 NRS and 5 NRS-drug. Except 
on SDNN, these variables are known to be s uitable for very 
short-term (≤ 1 minute) analysis of HRV [2]. Derived result 
was statistically validated with Wilcoxon test and Bonferroni 
correction. 
III. RESULT AND DISCUSSION 
The significant difference was not found between BL and 
5 NRS. This result means that the time domain variables of 
HRV are not a robust indicator of nociceptive pain. Otherwise, 
significant difference (p<0.0017) was found between BL and 
5 NRS -RF in some variables (AVNN, SDSD, RMSSD and 
pNN50). This result could be interpreted as the negative 
chronotropic effect of remifentanil[3] rather than the effect of 
nociceptive pain stimuli. 
IV. CONCLUSION 
In this research, we showed that the time domain variables 
of HRV are not a strong indicator of nociceptive pain. 
However, this research has some limitations in terms of the 
numbers of participants and the age band. To suggest 
generalized result, further studies are required based on 
enlarging participants. 
REFERENCES

indices for very short -term (30 beat) analysis. Part 1: survey and 
toolbox," Journal of Clinical Monitoring and Computing, vol. 27, pp. 
569-576, Oct 2013.

982-989, Oct 2005.
